newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil fin min says has no wage hike studies.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fin min says has no wage hike studies.

text.p: A spokesman for Finance Minister Pedro Malan said the Finance Ministry had not carried out any studies on raising public sector wages next year.
"We have no studies on this in the ministry," he said.
Jornal do Brasil newspaper reported Wednesday that the political decision to hike civil servants' wages from January 1 had already been taken after two years of no increases.
Jornal do Brasil said the level of the increase had not yet been set but that it would have to be lower than the expected rise in tax receipts in 1997.
Officials at the Administration Ministry, responsible for the civil service, could not be reached for comment.
Brasilia last raised public sector wages in January 1995 by 22 percent. Jornal do Brasil said 1995 inflation came in at 14.8 percent, giving civil servants a real increase in wages.
